verdict.label: BUY MEDIUM — PCE Absorbed; Iran MoU Compresses Oil Risk
verdict.rationale_short: S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at new records (7,563.63 and 26,917.47) as April PCE core printed at consensus (3.3% YoY, +0.2% MoM below the 0.3% estimate) and US-Iran negotiators agreed on a 60-day ceasefire MoU. Brent crude fell from an intraday high of $96.57 to a close of $93.71 as deal optimism spread, powerfully reactivating the XLE short thesis in a single session. Medium conviction: PCE headline at 3.8% YoY (3-year high) gives Warsh's hawkish committee live ammunition for June 16-17, and Dell's -3.93% after-hours decline on a record $43.8B beat introduces sell-the-news risk into AI infrastructure names.

bear_case: April PCE headline at 3.8% YoY — the highest since May 2023 — hands Warsh's 8-4 hawkish committee the hottest inflation print since he took the chair; core at 3.3% marks the third consecutive month above 3.0%, a pattern that historically precedes rate hike cycles, and the Fed chair who entered with a hawkish 8-4 vote now has a politically viable argument for a June 16-17 rate hike that would void every BUY thesis built on rate-stability expectations. Dell's -3.93% after-hours decline on $43.8B revenue (+88% YoY) and $24.4B in AI orders — following SNOW's pop-then-fade — signals the AI infrastructure complex is in a priced-for-perfection phase where record beats compress multiples rather than expand them. The Iran 60-day MoU is still pending Trump's signature, and the President has publicly stated he is 'not satisfied' with the current terms; rejection sends Brent back toward $100+ overnight, voids the XLE short, and re-inflates the Hormuz risk premium in a single session. If SPX loses 7,460 on a daily close and the 30Y closes above 5.10%, the BUY call converts to Step Aside immediately.
